purpose: Supplemental operational truth set for newly completed, clearly confirmed Sundowner events identified after the peer-reviewed/historical catalog was generated. Fire association remains a separate outcome field and is never the meteorological event definition.

pressure.interpretation: offshore/northerly support across the Santa Ynez Range

thermodynamics.temperature_context: hotter than normal regional conditions; exact event-zone observed maxima not recovered from trusted archival sources in this run

upstream_context.notes: No sufficiently specific, trusted archived station values for these upstream sectors were recovered in this run; fields intentionally remain null rather than inferred.

upper_air_model_context.pattern: 597-dam upper high centered over the Texas/Oklahoma Panhandles with a weak trough over California; moderate to strong east-west onshore gradient and a diurnally offshore north-south gradient
upper_air_model_context.source: NWS LOX Area Forecast Discussion issued 2026-07-27/28

events.fire_outcome_notes: No trusted Santa Barbara County incident source located that tied a wildfire ignition or spread episode to this wind event.

sources.evidence: Winds across southwest Santa Barbara County were observed gusting 35 to 45 mph, strongest near Refugio and Gaviota; the north-south pressure gradient was forecast/observed peaking near -3.7 mb at 8 PM, and a Wind Advisory was issued through 3 AM.
Elevated fire weather across southwest Santa Barbara County through the night due to gusty Sundowner winds and low humidities; RH 8-20 percent with poor overnight recovery.

events.notes: This is a genuinely new operationally confirmed event not present in data/known-sundowner-events.json or the 57-record historical reconstruction library as of 2026-08-05. It is retained separately until a complete reanalysis/station reconstruction can be generated without inventing unavailable upstream observations.
